procon-2026 viewer · design proposals · v5

Interaction / UX proposal

State models and interaction rules for the surfaces a contest team reads under time pressure: the replay transport, the SVG⇄WebGPU renderer switch, the live status HUD, and the map’s data marks. Every state below is anchored to a data-testid from the retired UI (PR #266); these names are proposed rebuild contracts; live values come from e2e/fixtures/match-state.snapshot.json.

01

State model — replay transport

Authority: createReplayStore (stores/replay.ts) owns currentStep / isPlaying / rate; the status label is derived, never stored. The UI never invents a second truth — the disable set of every control is a pure function of (currentStep, stepCount). Below: the state graph, the per-control contract per state, and the event table.

Invariants

  • One authority. createReplayStore is the single source of truth. Controls render from the snapshot; none of them derives play state independently (interaction-state: state authority).
  • Mutual exclusion. status is derived: playing XOR {idle, paused, finished}. finished requires stepCount-1 > 0 — single-step replays never reach S3 (observed guard in stores/replay.ts status()).
  • Orthogonal overlays. S4 (scrubbing) and S5 (rate) never replace the base state. S4 exists precisely to forbid the impossible combination the current code allows: a drag that the timer overwrites on its next tick.
  • Disable set is pure. Derived from (currentStep, stepCount) only — never from rate, theme, or renderer mode.
  • Single-slot timer. The effect clears the previous interval before arming (ReplayViewer.tsx:58–75); rate spam cannot stack intervals.
  • Rapid input is normal path. Step ± while playing does not pause; the timer continues from the new step. Pause then Play within one tick resumes from the same step.
  • Transient ≠ state. S5 has identical interaction rules to any other state — modelled as feedback so it cannot produce a phantom state.
02

Renderer switch — SVG ⇄ WebGPU

The segmented control on /solvers (solvers-renderer-svg / solvers-renderer-webgpu) picks a renderer; WebGpuMapViewer decides what is actually painted. Those two answers can disagree — and under headless SwiftShader they do, silently. This section defines every branch, including the one the current code has no name for.

Known bug — Issue #259. The WebGPU canvas renders blank under headless SwiftShader (docs/evidence/258/README.md:14–16, visible in target/uishots2/3-solvers-webgpu.png as an empty 800×420 region). The GPU path initializes fine, so no fallback and no loading branch is shown — the user gets an empty box and no signal. This proposal gives that outcome a designed state: data-fallback-reason="blank-frame".

Live status lifecycle

/live polls /match-state.json once per second (DEFAULT_POLL_MS = 1000, lib/live.ts). The badge carries the match phase; a second, orthogonal signal carries feed health. Both are needed: a match can be RUNNING on a dead feed, and that is the dangerous case.

BadgeWire statusPrimer semantic role (theme-resolved)MeaningUser action
— (none yet — STATUS_PLACEHOLDER, Live.tsx:71) fgColor.muted First poll has not resolved. Poll period 1000 ms; treat as empty after 5 × 1000 ms — check public/match-state.json exists.
Idle waiting fgColor.attention Day window has not opened yet (classifyStatus). None. Confirm the coordinator start time if the day is overdue.
Running running fgColor.success Within the day window; revisions are being accepted. Watch the HUD. No action.
Completed completed fgColor.accent Match finished (terminal). Go to /replays and review.
Error rejected / error fgColor.danger Submission rejected or coordinator error; snapshot.error is set. Read the live-error message (role="alert") and check CLI output.

04

Keyboard & focus

Tab moves between meaningful components; composites own their internal keys (keyboard-interface: page traversal ≠ component-internal navigation). Every action stays reachable without shortcuts — shortcuts are an optional acceleration layer, documented in the UI, never a hidden requirement.

Focus ring spec (v2 — button tone, not the accent)

  • Token references: outline: var(--borderWidth-thick) solid var(--borderColor-emphasis); offset var(--borderWidth-thin). No accent focus ring.
  • Functional requirement: verify the focus indicator against the actual bgColor.default and bgColor.muted backgrounds in both themes; non-text contrast must be at least 3:1. Earlier custom-palette measurements do not apply.
  • Clipped map viewport: use var(--focus-outline-offset) to keep the ring inside.
  • Never animate the ring (0ms) — it must appear in the same frame as focus.
  • Never use :focus — a mouse click must not leave a ring on a button.
  • Disabled controls keep the native disabled look (opacity: .45, replay-viewer.css:136–139) and leave the tab sequence — correct for plain buttons.

Same control, four states side by side — judge the contrast relationship here

Rest: borderWidth.thin / borderColor.default; hover: borderColor.emphasis; focus: borderWidth.thick / borderColor.emphasis. 両テーマの実背景で contrast を検証する。

  2. app-sidebar links — Home, Replays, Solvers, Live (nav landmark)
  3. [proposed] map-viewer-svg — one composite stop: arrows pan, +/− zoom, 0 resets camera
  4. replay-step-back

  8. replay-scrub

Stops today 8 → proposed 7 (map +1, rates −2).

Composite model (unchanged from v1 — keyboard behaviour was accepted)

  • Transport buttons: native <button>, activation via Enter/Space.
  • Rate group: APG radio-group — role="radiogroup"/radio, roving tabindex, arrows move, selection follows focus (no expensive side effect).
  • Map: one composite stop, arrow keys pan, +/− zoom, 0 reset; focus entry lands on the composite, not on each hex.
  • Overlay lifecycle (scrub drag): pointerdown suspends auto-advance; release restores the base state; Escape cancels a keyboard scrub back to the committed step.
  • Pointer and keyboard share one active model — dragging the scrub updates the same currentStep the arrow keys write.

Rule: if Kobalte has the primitive, take the primitive and skin it with Primer classes (@primer/css) — never rebuild its behaviour. If it does not (transport state machine, scrub overlay, frame probe, poller), implement in Solid and keep the state tables above as the contract.

Discoverability. Persistent hint line under the transport (same treatment as map-viewer__hint): Space play/pause · ← → step · 1 2 4 rate. Keyboard-only path = Tab → Enter/Space on the native buttons; no action is shortcut-only.

06

Map layer boundary — marks live in visualizer.html

The visualiser marks (terrain / spot-series / agent motifs) and every map colour assignment are not specified here — they belong to visualizer.html (motif-first marks, data-vis hue families for terrain/series/agent). This sheet only fixes where the state model touches the mark layer, so the two artifacts cannot contradict each other.

State-model touchpoints into the mark layer (implementation contract)
TouchpointState authorityWhat the mark layer must expose
map-viewer-svg composite one tab stop (section 04) marks rendered under role="img" + <title> built from matchId / turn; no per-hex focus
scrub overlay replay-scrub S4 orthogonal overlay (section 01) mark layer follows currentStep only; never a second truth about position
renderer switch (section 02) mode() / effective renderer SVG and WebGPU paint the same marks — identical motif paths, series % 6 cycling, keyline rule
blank-frame fallback (Issue #259) frame probe SVG fallback paints the same marks — fallback changes the painter, never the encoding
movement highlight derived from currentStep diff transient overlay only (motion table: 0 ms); encoding owned by visualizer.html
Token rule. Map marks take data-vis hues from @primer/primitives (emphasis = marker/boundary, muted = terrain fill) — no map colour literal is defined in this sheet or in app CSS. UI status semantics (section 03) use fgColor.* / bgColor.*, never data-vis (Primer rule: data hues are not semantic colours).
07

Motion spec

Level: functional minimal (brief). Motion exists only where it carries state change, continuity, or feedback — and never above 150ms. Feedback stays under 100ms so repeated clicks never queue. This spec was not revised in v2; it is restated so the new focus ring and badge treatments inherit the same rules.

Motion vocabulary (component-level; colour/type tokens are Primer’s own)

--m-feedback: 90ms · --m-state: 120ms · --m-swap: 140ms · --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) · --ease-linear: linear (progress fill only)

Motion table — element, property, duration, easing, trigger, reduced-motion
ElementPropertyDurationEasingTriggerprefers-reduced-motion

Scrub drag (pointer)thumb / fill0ms—pointermove — must track the pointer0ms (direct manipulation)
Scrub keyboard stepfill60msease-out←/→ on the range0ms

Absent by design (brief — motion where useful only)

  • Page / route transitions · map ambient animation · scroll effects
  • Hover lift or scale · badge pulse · skeleton shimmer (static skeleton bars only)
  • Loading spinner — use the existing webgpu-map-loading line or static skeletons

Reduced-motion: crossfade 140 ms → 0 ms (instant swap) · feedback colour retained · focus ring untouched. Enforced on this sheet by @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

08

Accessibility checklist

Findings from auditing the real components — not a generic WCAG dump. Severity follows accessibility-audit (critical / serious / moderate = P0 / P1 / P2), ranked by task impact on the contest viewer’s primary workflow. Severity chips use the same neutral chip + tone marker construction as the status badges (section 03).

Findings — source, impact, fix
SeverityFinding (source)ImpactFix
Critical · P0 Map has no keyboard or AT path. map-viewer-svg (MapViewer.tsx:190–203) handles wheel + pointer only; no tabindex, no role/<title>; the only hint (map-viewer__hint, :268) says “drag to pan, wheel to zoom”. WCAG 2.1.1, 1.1.1. The defining content of the product is pointer-only. Keyboard and screen-reader users get an unlabelled graphic they cannot move. One focusable composite stop (arrows pan, +/− zoom, 0 reset), role="img" + <title> from the HUD (matchId / turn), hint text lists the keys; the scores table remains the text alternative.
Critical · P0 Silent blank WebGPU canvas. Once renderer() is set (WebGpuMapViewer.tsx:138–141), neither webgpu-map-fallback nor webgpu-map-loading renders; under headless SwiftShader the canvas paints nothing (Issue #259; docs/evidence/258/README.md:14–16, target/uishots2/3-solvers-webgpu.png). Primary content vanishes with zero signal — no status, no announcement, no error. Frame probe (readback after 10 rAF / 400ms) → data-fallback-reason="blank-frame" + SVG fallback + role="status" strip (section 02).
Serious · P1 Stale data passes as live. fetchLiveSnapshot returns null on any failure and the poller only writes on success (lib/live.ts:130–142, 314–317), so the badge keeps showing RUNNING over an old LAST UPDATE; live-error never fires (it renders snapshot-borne error only, Live.tsx:163–169). An operator reads a dead feed as a live match — the most dangerous failure in a timed contest. lastSuccessAt + STALE badge at ≥5× poll interval + role="status" announcement (section 03).
Serious · P1 Announced renderer ≠ rendered renderer. aria-pressed follows requested mode() (Solvers.tsx:82–95) while WebGpuMapViewer silently falls back to SVG; fallback/loading have no live region (WebGpuMapViewer.tsx:193–206). AT reports “WebGPU pressed” over SVG pixels; the fallback transition is unannounced. aria-pressed tracks the effective renderer; data-degraded chip keeps the requested one; role="status" on fallback + loading.
Moderate · P2 Rate selector is an exclusive choice marked as three independent toggles. role="group" + per-button aria-pressed (ReplayViewer.tsx:167–181); no composite keyboard model. AT cannot convey “one of three selected”; arrow keys do nothing inside the group. APG radio-group: role="radiogroup" / radio, aria-checked, roving tabindex + arrows. Visual unchanged.
Moderate · P2 Scrub value announced without context. Native range (ReplayViewer.tsx:185–202) has no aria-valuetext; visible copy is “step 1 / 5” but AT reads a bare number. Explicit aria-valuemin/max/now duplicate native defaults. Position in the replay is ambiguous for AT users. aria-valuetext="Step 1 of 5"; drop the redundant value attributes.
Moderate · P2 Hardcoded id="replay-scrub" (ReplayViewer.tsx:185). A second viewer instance duplicates the id; the <label for> binds to the first only. Broken label association as soon as two replays share a page. useId() per instance.
Moderate · P2 Renderer segment has no designed focus/selected treatment. No rule exists for .page__renderer-btn anywhere in src/styles/; screenshot shows raw UA buttons (uishots2/3). Keyboard focus on the segment is inconsistent with every other control. Same :focus-visible ring as section 04 (borderWidth.thick / borderColor.emphasis / offset borderWidth.thin) + [aria-pressed=true] fill as replay-viewer__rate-btn.
Moderate · P2 Match phase changes are silent to AT. live-status-badge is a plain span (Live.tsx:125–127); RUNNING→COMPLETED/REJECTED is never announced. Screen-reader users miss the single most important event on the live page. role="status" container (polite); keep the text label — colour is never the only cue.
Moderate · P2 Heading level changes per route. Live uses <h1> (Live.tsx:123) while Solvers/Replays use <h2> for the same slot (Solvers.tsx:63, Replays.tsx:43); viewer title is <h3> (ReplayViewer.tsx:90). Inconsistent heading navigation across routes. Page title = h1 everywhere; viewer title h2/h3 consistently.
Moderate · P2 Score table semantics + alignment. No <caption>; player cells are <td> (not row headers); every cell is text-align: left (replay-viewer.css:87–103) so score digits do not align. Comparison is harder than it needs to be; table semantics are incomplete. Per section 09 / table-design: <th scope="row"> player, right-align + tabular-nums score, caption naming the match, two-tier type.
Moderate · P3 Disabled transport signalled by opacity: .45 alone (replay-viewer.css:136–139); no explanation at boundaries (step-back at start, step-forward at end). Boundary states are only inferable from the counter. Keep native disabled; pair with the counter (“1 / 5”) and a title reason (“Already at first step”).
09

Score table spec — alice / bob

Per table-design: the task is read + compare two player scores at the current step — lookup/comparison, no cell selection or editing → a native <table>, not an interactive grid. The 2D structure is preserved; there is nothing to recompose.

Column rules

  • Row identity: player id (alice / bob) as <th scope="row">.
  • Caption: Scores — demo-match (state().matchId.value, ReplayViewer.tsx:109).
  • player — left-aligned, text; score — right-aligned, integer, no unit, font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, precision fixed per column.
  • Type: two tiers only (v2). Labels (caption, column heads) at 11px; values (player name, score) at 15px. No third size for “emphasis” — the score’s priority comes from right alignment and column position, not a larger font.
  • Missing value: em dash — (same discipline as STATUS_PLACEHOLDER, Live.tsx:71). Never an empty cell.
  • No delta column. F1-style red/green deltas are explicitly out of the brief’s colour discipline (DESIGN-BRIEF, References — do not copy).
  • Density: row height base.size.32, borderWidth.thin / borderColor.default row divider, no zebra, no hover chrome — 2 rows, read-only.
  • Growth: if players > 8 rows, sticky thead inside the table’s own scroll region (never hide the scrollbar).

UI の見た目は @primer/css の class、トークンは @primer/primitives の参照を使用する。 この単一 HTML は配布 CSS の使用トークンを embed-primer.py で機械抽出して埋め込む。 埋め込み領域は自動生成であり、アプリケーションの CSS へ値を書き写さない。 符号と地図色は visualizer.html、shell は layout.html を正とする。

例外 EXC-UX-TYPE: 引き継ぎ資料で固定された HUD / score の label 11px + value 15px は Primer に同じ組がないため維持する。他の文字サイズは Primer typography を参照する。 SVG 状態図の座標・viewBox・注記文字サイズと文書の幅は図とレイアウトの幾何であり、UI トークンではない。 Motion の時間はこの interaction spec で定義する。

この提案のデモは vanilla JS で状態モデルを示す。Kobalte 自体の動作確認は PR #270 の PrimerSpike.tsx に属する。a11y 表の既存コードへの行参照は PR #266 撤去前の所見であり、再構築時の受け入れ条件として残す。
